question: This is a topographic map of a real place (Bear Mountain, New York), drawn in the style of a USGS 7.5-minute quadrangle. The contour interval is 20 meters, index contours (heavy brown lines, some labeled) are every 100 meters, and elevations are in meters. Flash flood: the dam at the magenta square D has failed. The water runs downhill from D, always in the direction of steepest descent, so its path crosses every contour line at a right angle. 6 campsites are marked with magenta points, C1 to C6, all lower than the dam. Exactly one of them lies in the water's path. Which campsite does the water reach? Answer with the campsite name, for example C2.
references: USGS 7.5-minute topographic quadrangle maps (US Topo, 1:24 000): brown contours, heavy index contours
Elevation: USGS 3D Elevation Program (3DEP, public domain) via AWS Open Data Terrain Tiles (terrarium, zoom 13); surface water runs down the line of steepest descent, at right angles to the contours
